full_judgment:
2. The relevant fact necessary for the disposal of the present Rule is that plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1-5 filed Title Suit No. 87 of 1985 before the Munsif, 3rd Court, Com ilia for simple declaration of title of the suit land described in the 2nd schedule to the plaint. The aforesaid suit was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 26 of 1991. Plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1-5 filed the above suit in the background when they disclosed their intention to make construction on the suit land the defendant-petitioners made adverse claim of the title over the suit land. 

 3. Immediately after filing of the suit plaintiff- opposite party Nos. 1-5 filed an application for temporary injunction on 27-2-85 for restraining the defendant-petitioners from interfering with their possession of the suit land. Accordingly, the trial Court granted ad-interim injunction vide order dated 18-8-85 against the defendant-petitioners ex parte. Subsequently, injunction matter was contested by the defendant-petitioners and the trial Court after hearing both the parties passed an order of status-quo vide order dated 22-9-85 modifying the order of ad-interim injunction. Subsequently plaintiff- opposite parties being in need of repair of their kachcha structures standing on the suit land obtained an order of repair from the trial Court on 22-2-86. The defendant-petitioners being aggrieved by the said order of repair challenged the same by filing Civil Revision No. 120 of 1986 before the High Court Division. Eventually, a Single Bench of the High Court Division by order dated 2-12-87 set aside the aforesaid order of repair apparently on the ground that the 2nd schedule did not mention about any structure standing on the suit land. In this background of the matter plaintiff-opposite parties filed an application for amendment of the plaint on 18-3-90. 

 4. The trial Courtallowed the amendment vide order dated 29-4-90. It is important to note in this connection that the defendant-petitioners neither filed any written objection against the prayer for amendment of the plaint nor was present when the application for amendment was heard. Rather the defendant-petitioners filed additional written statement on 23-10-90 in view of the amendment of the plaint. Long after the amendment of the plaint as mentioned above defendant-petitioners filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for mandatory injunction for removing the plaintff-opposite parties from the suit hut. The trial Court after hearing both the parties refused to grant mandatory injunction BY the impugned order dated 10-2-92 mainly on the ground that since the plaintiff-opposite parties made out positive case by way of amendment that they were living in the kachcha hut standing on the suit land there cannot be any mandatory injunction for removal of the plaintiff-opposite parties without any evidence that the plaintiffs took over possession of the suit hut by violating the order of status-quo, more so when the defendant-petitioners were allowed to amend the plaint on this point without contesting the same. 

 5. Mr Abdul Kuddus Miah, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners, submits that the trial Court was not justified in allowing the amendment of the plaint in spite of the fact that the defendant-petitioners failed to contest the same inasmuch as the amendment altered the nature and character of the suit. With regard to inordinate delay in filing the present revisional application the learned Lawyer for the defendant-petitioners submits that the period of limitation should be taken to run from 10-2-92 on which date the prayer for mandatory injunction was refused and not from 29-4-90 being the date of amendment inasmuch as the date of amendment should be considered to have merged in the order dated 10-2-92 as the mandatory injunction was refused on that date mainly on the ground that the amendment was not challenged. It is further submitted by the learned lawyer for the defendant-petitioners that since the plaintiff-opposite parties took over possession of the suit hut by violating the order of status quo the trial Court ought to have granted mandatory injunction directing to remove plaintiff No.3 from the suit hut. The learned Advocate in this connection referred to two decisions reported in 35 DLR (AD) 42 and 47 DLR 170 on the scope of mandatory injunction. 

 6. Me Syed Mahmud Hossain, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that the present-revisional application is. hopelessly time-barred inasmuch as the defendant-petitioners filed the revision after an inordinate delay of more than 500 days from the date of first impugned order dated 29-4-90 i.e. the date of amendment. With regard to the impugned order dated 10-2-92 refusing mandatory injunction, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties submits that since there is no evidence on record that the plaintiffs entered into and occupied the suit hut by force violating order of status-quo, the trial Court rightly refused to grant mandatory injunction, more so when the amendment of the plaint on this aspect was allowed without contest. 

 8. Mandatory injunction is highly discretionary relief and is granted in favour of the aggrieved party only when it is proved that the offending party has committed an illegal act in relation to the subject matter of the suit in violation of a legal right of a party in the suit. In the present case the plaintiff-opposite parties made out a case on the basis of their original plaint and also by way of amendment of the plaint that plaintiff No. 3 is in occupation of a suit hut from before unless there is evidence on this factual aspect that the plaintiff No. 3 was not in possession of the suit hut at the time of filing the suit and he took over possession of the same subsequently by force by violating the order of status-quou. cannot be said that the defendant petitioners made out a prima facie arguable case for mandatory injunction for removing plaintiff No.3 from the suit hut, more so when amendment of the plaint was never contested and it was rather accepted by filing additional written statement. In this background of the case, there is no justification to interfere with the impugned order dated 10-2-92 refusing mandatory injunction.
